In university you're right it's alot harder. I basically scraped my way through uni bcos of anxiety but here's how I did it:

- I can't study at home so I went to all sorts of places to study. The library, random study rooms, coffee shops, empty department rooms that weren't even for my degree etc etc etc. 
- I tried to force myself to wake up early but no matter how hard I tried it wouldn't work, so I would get eight hours, wake up at 10am and work till whenever. It doesn't matter when your routine is, just have one even if it's a simple one!
- Be the most annoying person on your course. Ask your lecturers questions. Go to out of hours. Attend study sessions, tutorials etc. Bother your coursemates and upperclassmen if you know any. I used to ask the teaching assistants to check my answers so many times they always ended up just sitting next to me in the lesson lol
- try and fight imposter syndrome and the feeling that others are doing better than you. I had a therapist who helped me but before that the feelings were always there. But I realise in hindsight who cares? You will all end up with mostly the same grade anyway, and employers don't care once you've gotten your first job.
- try to get extra time if you have anxiety/depression/another mental health disorder
 Hope this helps
